headline: Oil prices jump 2% as US and Iran trade fire in Middle East
summary: The US attacked Iranian rocket launchers on Larak island, prompting Iran to retaliate with ballistic missiles targeting US bases in Jordan.
details: The United States and Iran have engaged in their first exchange of fire in a month, escalating tensions in a region already engulfed in a six-month conflict.
The US military's Central Command reported taking 'limited, precise action' against IRGC minelaying forces on Larak island to prevent Tehran from planting mines in the Strait of Hormuz.
In retaliation, Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed to have struck two US air bases in Jordan with ballistic missiles, causing 'heavy damage'.
Jordan's army stated it intercepted eight missiles, while Iran also claimed to have targeted US personnel in the UAE and shot down an American drone over Hormuz.
The UAE dismissed claims of an attack on Al Minhad Air Base as 'baseless', though it confirmed dealing with a drone over its waters.
The conflict centers on control of the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic waterway where one-fifth of the world's oil passes. Iran has blocked commercial shipping since the war began.
Global oil prices rose by at least two percent on Monday following the strikes, reflecting concerns over energy security and supply disruptions.
Despite previous ceasefire agreements in April and June, the two nations remain at an impasse, with Washington now prioritizing 'economic warfare' and expanded sanctions.
caption:

In retaliation, Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed to have struck two US air bases in Jordan with ballistic missiles, causing 'heavy damage'.

Jordan's army stated it intercepted eight missiles, while Iran also claimed to have targeted US personnel in the UAE and shot down an American drone over Hormuz.

The UAE dismissed claims of an attack on Al Minhad Air Base as 'baseless', though it confirmed dealing with a drone over its waters.

The conflict centers on control of the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic waterway where one-fifth of the world's oil passes. Iran has blocked commercial shipping since the war began.

Global oil prices rose by at least two percent on Monday following the strikes, reflecting concerns over energy security and supply disruptions.

Despite previous ceasefire agreements in April and June, the two nations remain at an impasse, with Washington now prioritizing 'economic warfare' and expanded sanctions.

headline: Father allegedly sold toddler for Tk 1 lakh to buy iPhone
summary: A 22-year-old man in Patuakhali has been detained after he allegedly sold his 1.5-year-old son for money to purchase a new smartphone.
details: A 22-year-old man named Maruf Munshi has been detained by Dashmina Police in Patuakhali after allegations that he sold his 1.5-year-old son for approximately Tk 1 lakh.

The child was rescued from the Char Biswas area of Galachipa Upazila. According to the family, Maruf sold the child to Mohibul, the father-in-law of his colleague Imran Hossain, who does not have any sons.

The family claims that Maruf took an advance of Tk 52,000 and signed a written agreement to hand over the child. They allege he used this money, along with the value of his old iPhone, to buy a new iPhone.

Maruf, who works as a mason in Dhaka, has denied the allegations of selling his son. He told police that he gave the child to his colleague and the colleague's father-in-law for upbringing due to his own debts.
Police OC Atikul Islam stated that since the family has not yet filed a written complaint, legal action against the involved parties has faced some complications.
The police are now coordinating with the Upazila administration and the Department of Women and Children Affairs to determine the next steps.

The family claims that Maruf took an advance of Tk 52,000 and signed a written agreement to hand over the child. They allege he used this money, along with the value of his old iPhone, to buy a new iPhone.

Maruf, who works as a mason in Dhaka, has denied the allegations of selling his son. He told police that he gave the child to his colleague and the colleague's father-in-law for upbringing due to his own debts.

Police OC Atikul Islam stated that since the family has not yet filed a written complaint, legal action against the involved parties has faced some complications.
